notes: Units were aligned by anchor position in the saved text (overlap of at least 30 percent of the shorter anchor), plus 10 hand-made pairs where the coders quoted different spans of one sentence. Main disagreements: (1) phase, mostly general vs during-work or before-course for Do/Don't items, benefit statements and design advice; resolved by the phase definitions (facts and principles stay general, acts done while using AI go to during-work, set-up and design go to before-course, misuse reporting goes to when-misuse). (2) unit_stance on benefit statements and compliance duties (encourage/neutral, neutral/restrict); resolved by whether the sentence takes a position on AI use itself (conditions on use are restrict, benefit claims under a pro-AI document encourage, bare compliance duties neutral). (3) modality should vs informs/must, resolved by the sentence's own verb. (4) policy_type split in the research and HR sections (P62 vs P50/P52/P53/P70/P76), resolved to the more specific type when the sentence is about data, IP, bias, training or HR operations; P61 kept for scope sentences. Only-B units are mostly research-section statements (coder A skipped much of it); all kept except two link-text fragments. Only-A units kept after re-reading. In the CISE page coder A split one sentence into two rules; both kept. Both coders gave stance delegates, delegates, restrict.
